claims.text: CRISIL's annexure row for ISIN INE001A07RW5 lists a 7.87% coupon, allotment on 18 July 2019, scheduled maturity on 18 July 2022, and an issue size of Rs 5,000 crore.
claims.locator: S1 annexure row for ISIN INE001A07RW5

claims.text: The FY20 MD&A reports standalone total income of Rs 58,763 crore and profit after tax of Rs 17,770 crore, and Rs 46,437 crore of secured redeemable NCDs raised at issuer level.
claims.locator: S4 MD&A, FY20 standalone performance and borrowings
claims.excerpt: standalone total income of Rs 58,763 crore

claims.text: The stated tenor is 1,096 days, approximately three calendar years, derived from the 18 July 2019 allotment and 18 July 2022 scheduled maturity.
Three scheduled annual coupons at 7.87% would sum to 23.61% of principal over the stated tenor; this is not a yield and assumes scheduled payments.
The FY20 MD&A states the NCDs are listed on the NSE/BSE wholesale debt market.
Listing is not the same as executable secondary liquidity; the record contains no price, yield, or liquidity data.
AAA/Stable is a rating opinion dated 31 July 2020, not a guarantee and not a current rating.
The +200bp rate move and risk-off secondary-market scenario is demo-authored for this replay; it is not a forecast or issuer guidance.
claims.excerpt: +200bp rate move and risk-off secondary market

claims.text: The meeting record contains no executable price, yield, or secondary-market liquidity data for the series.
claims.locator: Shared fact sheet, What is not established
claims.excerpt: No executable price, yield, or secondary-market liquidity

claims.text: Scheduled maturity is 18 July 2022; the meeting does not assert that payment occurred.
claims.locator: Shared fact sheet, What is not established

claims.text: The rating annexure describes the instrument as a debenture; the retained excerpt does not establish series-level secured or unsecured status.
The outcome is a research checklist, not a buy/sell recommendation or investment approval.
claims.locator: Shared fact sheet, Outcome and limitations
claims.excerpt: research checklist, not a buy/sell recommendation

claims.text: A prepared path may open with a downside review before the credit fact pack; the evidence set does not change.
A prepared path may open with the portfolio mandate so the missing market inputs are visible before the credit discussion.
The liquidity follow-up asks whether the listed debenture can be sold before maturity without assuming a price or a buyer.
The covenant follow-up asks which contractual protections would survive a rating downgrade; the record does not supply the covenant package.
The red-team turn tests whether the research checklist claims more than the retained evidence supports.

prepared_turns.label: You
prepared_turns.question: Portfolio Analyst, assume a fictional three-year mandate that requires an executable price, yield, and liquidity assessment. What can you conclude from this record?
